name: Diamond Ledger
subtitle: an archive written in diamond's carbon isotopes

effects.effect: molecules shift the colour of light they scatter

effect: molecules shift the colour of light they scatter
how: Every storage medium we use, from disks to tape, has to be copied every few decades or the data fades. Here bits are grown into a synthetic diamond as tiny regions of ordinary or heavy carbon, which never decay or wander; a laser reads them because the heavier carbon shifts the colour of the light the diamond scatters.
obstacle: Growing diamond layer by layer in isotope patterns is slow and costly, so it stores far less per dollar than tape.
why: Isotope-layered diamond is made for quantum sensors; never used as an archive.
real: No isotope-patterned (12C/13C) diamond storage read by Raman shift was found; diamond storage work uses NV/ND1 defects, and 13C Raman barcodes have been shown only in polymers.
